blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A participant that verifies PINs calls an HSM. When the HSM call times out it catches the exception, logs it and returns FAIL. AnswerFailures from this unit stands right before SendResponse. What does the terminal receive for those purchases?

options.text: A 96, since the timeout left no failure in the Result for AnswerFailures to map
options.says: rcFor finds no failure in the Result and falls back to 96, system malfunction

options.text: A 55, since the timeout is recorded in the Result as a PIN failure by FAIL
options.says: FAIL is only a vote; nothing is recorded in the Result unless the participant calls fail, and the PIN was never checked

options.text: No answer, since a timeout answered with FAIL leaves AnswerFailures nothing to do
options.says: AnswerFailures answers every abort that reaches it without a refusal already built

options.text: A 91, since the timeout is recorded in the Result as an unreachable host
options.says: 91 comes only from a HOST_UNREACHABLE failure someone recorded; FAIL is only a vote and records nothing, so the code is 96

origin.section: 10.1 A Response Code Says Who Failed, and One Participant Chooses It

questions.stem: A chain runs Authorize, which puts a 00 response in the Context, then a new fraud-scoring participant, then AnswerFailures in unit s5's version, then SendResponse. The scoring service is down and the scoring participant throws. What does the terminal receive?

options.text: A 96, since AnswerFailures replaces the 00 in the Context once the transaction aborts
options.says: s5's AnswerFailures sees a response already in the Context and leaves it; SendResponse sends whatever RESPONSE holds

options.text: No answer, since SendResponse drops the 00 in the Context once the transaction aborts
options.says: SendResponse sends RESPONSE from abort as from commit

options.text: A 00, since SendResponse sends the 00 in the Context once the transaction aborts
options.says: the approval stays in RESPONSE, s5's version keeps any response, and SendResponse sends it on the abort path

options.text: A 05, since the TransactionManager overwrites the 00 in the Context once the transaction aborts
options.says: the TransactionManager never touches RESPONSE; it logs the exception and counts an ABORTED vote

origin.section: 10.3 On the Abort Path `SendResponse` Sends Whatever `RESPONSE` Holds

questions.stem: A team moves the grown AnswerFailures to the top of the chain, before CheckFields, 'so that it sees every transaction'. A purchase now fails CheckFields with a missing field. What happens?

options.text: The terminal gets 30, since AnswerFailures is asked on the abort path wherever it stands
options.says: prepareForAbort reaches only the abort participants after the one that aborted; this one was prepared earlier and said NO_JOIN

options.text: The terminal gets 96, since AnswerFailures answered before CheckFields could report a cause
options.says: AnswerFailures answers nothing in prepare; it is never asked again, so it builds no 96 either

options.text: The terminal gets no answer, since AnswerFailures was prepared earlier and is not asked again
options.says: it voted NO_JOIN in prepare, and prepareForAbort goes only to abort participants after CheckFields

options.text: The terminal gets no answer, since CheckFields stops the chain before SendResponse is called
options.says: SendResponse is an abort participant after CheckFields and is still called; it finds no RESPONSE

origin.section: 10.3 On the Abort Path `SendResponse` Sends Whatever `RESPONSE` Holds

questions.stem: Terminal 29110044 sends a purchase with STAN 004210, which the server approves and records. The acquirer then sends an 0420 with STAN 004211, and after a lost answer an 0421 with STAN 004211. The server looks the original up by terminal, STAN and field 7. Which handling leaves the card's daily total right?

options.text: Look up STAN 004211 and field 7 of each message, since they are the fields the reversal itself carries
options.says: a reversal is a new message with its own STAN; the original's STAN and time are in field 90, so this finds nothing

options.text: Look up STAN 004210 from field 90 and remove the record, since a repeat must find nothing left to undo
options.says: field 90 names the original, and taking the record means the 0421 gives nothing back a second time

options.text: Look up STAN 004210 from field 90 and keep the record, since the 0421 must find the same purchase again
options.says: the repeat then gives the amount back a second time, and the total goes below what was spent

options.text: Look up STAN 004211 and decline the 0421, since a repeat of a reversal already answered is a duplicate
options.says: a repeat is answered like the first; a refusal leaves the acquirer's reversal open

origin.section: 10.4 A Reversal Is Answered `00`, Finds Its Original Through Field 90, and Undoes It Once

concepts: prepareForAbort reaches only abort participants after the one that aborted, so an answering participant placed earlier answers nothing.
